seo.title: Self-employed: what to deposit by 31.12
seo.description: Self-employed: the tax benefits on pension and study-fund deposits count by the year the money reached the fund. Check now how much was deposited this year and how much is missing up to the beneficial ceiling.
eyebrow: Self-employed · End of the tax year
title: By 31.12 — so you don't give up the tax benefit
intro: A self-employed person has no employer paying in for them — and so no one to remind them. The benefits on pension and study-fund deposits are money the state is willing to leave with you — provided you deposit in time.
p1.title: The benefit counts by the day the money reached the fund
p1.body: A deposit received on 2 January won't help in the return for the year that has ended. A transfer in the last days of December may only be received in January — mid-December is a reasonable safety margin.
p2.title: Pension fund: a credit and a deduction
p2.body: The deposit that makes full use of the benefit is about 16.5% of qualifying income — up to about ₪38,400 in 2026. The mandatory deposit for the self-employed is only the minimum.
p3.title: Study fund: a deduction and a tax-free withdrawal
p3.body: A deduction on deposits of 4.5% of income, up to ₪13,203 a year; up to ₪20,566 a year with an exemption from capital-gains tax on withdrawal.
caveat: The figures are for the 2026 tax year and are updated every year — confirm them with your accountant before transferring money.
guide: The full guide: what to deposit by 31 December
